literal: Hui then requested a private audience to discuss affairs and fully memorialized what he had heard, saying: "The former emperor moved the capital because the people were attached to their native soil; therefore he issued the edict of winter and summer dual residence, only to provisionally settle the people's will for the time being."
idiomatic: Hui then asked for a private audience, reported everything he had heard, and said: "The former emperor moved the capital because the people clung to their native soil; he issued the edict of winter and summer residence only to ease their minds for the moment."

literal: Those were words of the moment, not truly the former emperor's deeper intent.
idiomatic: That was the language of the hour—not the former emperor's true intent.

literal: Moreover, in recent years the migrants have lived in peace many years; public and private plans are settled, and they have no wish to return.
idiomatic: Moreover, the migrants have settled peacefully for years; households and the state have made their plans, and none wish to go back.

literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty will complete the enterprise the High Ancestor established—do not believe wicked ministers who say otherwise."
idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to finish what the High Ancestor fixed—do not heed wicked ministers who say it should not be so."

literal: The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

literal: Again promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Right Guard General.
idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Guard General.

literal: Though he brought no real benefit, he was deeply favored in intimacy.
idiomatic: Though he offered little real benefit, he was deeply favored.

literal: Whatever confidential matters within the forbidden precincts, Hui separately received edicts and stored them in a chest.
idiomatic: For every secret matter within the inner palace, Hui alone received the edicts and locked them in a chest.

literal: Only when Hui entered might it be opened; the rest of the attendants and yellow gates had no knowledge.
idiomatic: Only Hui, on entering, might open it; the other attendants and eunuchs knew nothing.

literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang also received gracious favor; therefore men of the time called them "Starved Hawk General, Hungry Eagle Attendant."
idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang was likewise showered with favor, so contemporaries dubbed them "the Starved Hawk General and the Hungry Eagle Attendant."

literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

literal: Accepting bribes for office—all had fixed prices: great commanderies two thousand bolts, middle commanderies one thousand, lower five hundred; other offices each had their differences; all under heaven called it the Market Bureau.
idiomatic: He sold offices at fixed rates—two thousand bolts for a great commandery, one thousand for a middle one, five hundred for a lower one, with other posts priced accordingly—and the realm called it the Market Bureau.

literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He left the capital as Inspector of Ji Province.

literal: On the day he left for the province he continuously loaded goods in carts; from Xindu to Tangyin the head and tail linked without break along the road.
idiomatic: The day he departed he sent cart after cart laden with goods; from Xindu to Tangyin the convoy never broke.

literal: When the carts lacked horn grease, he met oxen on the road and freshly cut off horns to fill the need.
idiomatic: When the wagons ran short of horn grease, he met oxen on the road and cut fresh horns to supply it.

literal: Hui inspected and mustered household registers, permitting return to chief registers; he issued a levy of fifty thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: Hui audited household registers, allowed men to return to their chief registers, and levied fifty thousand bolts of silk.

literal: Yet he amassed without limit—the people suffered.
idiomatic: Yet he extorted without end, and the people groaned under it.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming he was summoned as Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy; an edict made him act in Personnel selection affairs.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he was recalled as Left Deputy of the Secretariat and ordered to handle personnel selection.

literal: Later it was announced that Hui together with Prince of Rencheng Cheng, Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and Prince of Dongping Kuang would jointly decide great matters at the Gate Office.
idiomatic: Later an edict named Hui, together with the Princes of Rencheng, Jingzhao, and Dongping, to decide major affairs at the Gate Office.

literal: Hui again submitted a memorial discussing essentials of government: the first said the censor's office must obtain worthy men.
idiomatic: Hui again memorialized on the essentials of government. First: the censorate must secure worthy men.

literal: One must obtain the right man, not be bound by rank and grade; long in the matter, demand success.
idiomatic: Get the right man, not the right rank; keep him long in the post and hold him to results.

literal: The second said pacify the people and secure the borders, observe the time and then act.
idiomatic: Second: pacify the people and secure the borders—watch the moment, then move.

literal: In recent times border generals lack far-reaching strategy, greedy for one-in-ten-thousand merit; the good accord between Chu and Liang is unheard of, while the silkworm-woman's grievance is repeatedly tied—this is what petty men do, keen for treacherous profit.
idiomatic: Lately frontier commanders lack long vision and chase a sliver of glory; no one hears of harmony between Chu and Liang, yet the silkworm woman's grievance is tied again and again—petty men chasing illicit gain.

literal: The plan to pacify Wu has its own good design—not in one city one garrison.
idiomatic: The plan to pacify Wu has its own design; it is not a matter of one fortress, one garrison.

literal: Moreover several provinces of Hebei are the state's foundation;
idiomatic: Moreover, the Hebei provinces are the state's foundation;

literal: famine many years, households scattered in flight.
idiomatic: famine has lasted years, and households have fled and scattered.

literal: Now on the borders troops are again levied and sent—at a time like this, how easy to stir movement?
idiomatic: Now troops are levied and sent to the borders again—at such a time, how easy to stir unrest?

literal: I foolishly think that for several years past one should only quiet the borders to rest levies and summons, settle the people and encourage farming, show favor to central China.
idiomatic: I foolishly believe that for some years now we should only still the frontiers, ease levies and corvée, settle the people, and encourage farming—showing kindness to the heartland.

literal: I request sternly to admonish border generals: from now on those in garrison whom bandits ask to submit within—do not permit rashly to send relief and receive; all must be reported to the throne.
idiomatic: I ask that frontier commanders be sternly warned: from now on, when bandits in the garrisons offer submission, no one may rashly send troops to accept them—all must be reported to the throne.

literal: Violators though they have merit, I request they be judged by violation of edict.
idiomatic: Even if they have merit, violators should be punished for disobeying the edict.

literal: The third said the state's stores depend solely on Hebei.
idiomatic: Third: the state's stores depend entirely on Hebei.

literal: Famine accumulated years, households fled and scattered; grown crafty and deceitful, thereby producing concealment.
idiomatic: Years of famine drove households to flee; men grew cunning and hid their numbers.

literal: Shrinking the young and old, falsely registering death and loss, collecting people's rent and levies, cutting them into one's own pocket.
idiomatic: They shrank the rolls of young and old, falsely recorded deaths, collected rent and tax, and kept the cut for themselves.

literal: The people suffer below, the offices lose above.
idiomatic: The people suffered below; the state lost above.

literal: Unless one newly establishes empowering regulations, skillfully inspect and muster, the coming of loss and depletion has not yet ended.
idiomatic: Unless new rules are set and registers rigorously checked, the drain will not cease.

literal: I request discussion of this, clearly proclaiming regulations.
idiomatic: I ask that this be debated and the regulations clearly proclaimed.

literal: The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

literal: Hui by nature loved literature, gathered Confucian scholars Cui Hong and others to compile essentials of the hundred schools by category, named Collected Categories, in all two hundred seventy scrolls, from Fuxi above to Jin below, in all fourteen generations.
idiomatic: Hui loved letters by nature. He gathered scholars such as Cui Hong to compile essentials of the hundred schools by category into Collected Categories—270 scrolls from Fuxi down through Jin, fourteen dynasties in all.

literal: Hui gravely ill, memorialized and presented it.
idiomatic: When Hui fell gravely ill, he presented the work to the throne.

literal: He died; given Eastern Garden secret implements, posthumously Acting Holder of Staff, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies, Duke of the Work Minister, posthumous title Literary and Reverent.
idiomatic: He died. The court granted Eastern Garden funeral gear and posthumously named him Acting Staff Bearer, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies, and Duke of Works, with the posthumous title Literary and Reverent.

literal: At burial, given feather canopy, halberd escort, and twenty musicians; one hundred twenty feathered guards.
idiomatic: For the funeral he received a feathered canopy, halberd escort, twenty musicians, and 120 guards of the feathered forest.

literal: Son Bi, styled Zongfu, nature gentle and generous, beautiful bearing.
idiomatic: His son Bi, styled Zongfu, was gentle, generous, and handsome.

literal: As Emperor Zhuang's nephew by marriage, specially enfeoffed Viscount of Guangchuan.
idiomatic: As Emperor Zhuang's nephew by marriage, he was specially enfeoffed Viscount of Guangchuan.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianping he rose to Minister of the Secretariat.

literal: Bi's sister was taken by Emperor Xiaowu; because of kinship he was entrusted, favors exceptionally lofty.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu took Bi's sister as consort; trusting kinship, he heaped honors on Bi.

literal: He served as Director of the Secretariat, recorded Secretariat affairs, rank Exceptionally Advanced, Imperial Clan Mentor.
idiomatic: He became Director of the Secretariat, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs, Exceptionally Advanced, and Imperial Clan Mentor.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: When Qi took the mandate, he was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he died.
idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianbao.

literal: In the tenth year, his sons together with all the Yuans were executed to death.
idiomatic: In the tenth year his sons were executed along with the other Yuans.

literal: Bi's nephew's son Shijiang had clever ingenuity.
idiomatic: Bi's nephew Shijiang was ingeniously skilled.

literal: By the time of Qi Wucheng, post Commandant of the Palace Master of Construction.
idiomatic: Under Qi Wucheng he became Commandant of the Directorate of Palace Construction.

literal: De's younger brother Zan had considerable reputation, fond of stating military and state affairs.
idiomatic: De's younger brother Zan enjoyed a fine reputation and loved to discuss military and state affairs.

literal: When the Bureau of State was first established, Zan was made its inspector, granted noble rank Marquis of Shanggu.
idiomatic: When the State Inspectorate was first set up, Zan was made its inspector and enfeoffed Marquis of Shanggu.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen admonished Zan to transform the capital region: he could proclaim filial conduct, must make customs harmonious and rites and culture fully complete.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen charged Zan to civilize the capital region: proclaim filial piety, harmonize customs, and complete ritual and culture.

literal: From now on those unfilial and unfraternal—compare their gates, carve it on their gateposts.
idiomatic: Henceforth, households lacking filial piety or brotherly duty were to have the fact posted at their gates and carved on their gateposts.

literal: Also an edict said: "The State Bureau inspector's office is lofty and position weighty, duties summing the capital region, selection belonging to worthy kin, to fulfill the gaze of all."
idiomatic: An edict also said: "The State Inspector's post is lofty and weighty, overseeing the capital region. The choice must fall on a worthy kinsman who can meet the realm's expectations."

literal: But the princes are young, not yet versed in government principles, therefore it is given to Zan, hoping he can assist in guiding and transforming."
idiomatic: The princes are young and not yet versed in governance, so the post is given to Zan in hope he may help guide and transform them."

literal: Now the State Bureau is newly established, commanderies and counties newly founded, dukes and ministers downward all have their original posts, each may lead sons and younger brothers to extend mutual respect."
idiomatic: The State Inspectorate and its counties are newly founded. Every noble and minister still holds his former post; each should bring sons and younger kin to pay mutual respect."

literal: Thereupon he was granted the given name "Zan."
idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted the taboo name Zan.

literal: An edict made Zan ride a step-drawn carriage into the palace gate, added Heir Apparent Junior Tutor, promoted Left Deputy.
idiomatic: An edict allowed Zan to enter the palace gate in a hand-drawn carriage, named him Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and promoted him to Left Deputy.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen was about to plan moving the capital; the nobles mostly differed, only Zan approved the great plan.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen planned to move the capital, most princes objected; only Zan endorsed the great design.

literal: Each year when the emperor went south on campaign, he would take his hand and entrust later affairs.
idiomatic: Each year the emperor marched south, he would take Zan's hand and entrust him with affairs at home.

literal: He died; posthumously General Who Guards the States, Deputy as before.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Guards the States, retaining his deputy title.

literal: Later for Zan's merit assisting while remaining on guard, advanced enfeoffment to Count of Jinyang.
idiomatic: Later, for Zan's merit in staying behind to assist, his fief was raised to Count of Jinyang.

literal: Zan's younger brother Shu, styled Mairen.
idiomatic: Zan's younger brother Shu, styled Mairen.

literal: Bends a bow of three hundred jin, skilled at riding and shooting.
idiomatic: He could draw a three-hundred-jin bow and was skilled in riding and archery.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time, was Administrator of Hedong.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Administrator of Hedong.

literal: Hedong custom had many merchants, rarely pursued farming and sericulture; some reached thirty years without knowing the plow.
idiomatic: Hedong was full of traders who seldom farmed; some men reached thirty without ever touching a plow.

literal: Shu on taking office exhorted farming, personally went to teach and show; within two years every household had enough, men made a song of it: "Taizhou Hedong, shuttle replaces pounding."
idiomatic: On taking office Shu urged farming and taught the people himself. Within two years every household had enough, and they sang: "In Taizhou's Hedong the shuttle has replaced the pestle."

literal: When Duke Yuan arrived, the fields at last were put in order."
idiomatic: When Duke Yuan came, the fields were put in order at last."

literal: He died as General Who Pacifies the Plain City, posthumous title Tranquil.
idiomatic: He died as General Who Pacifies Pingcheng, posthumous title Tranquil.

literal: He had seven sons.
idiomatic: He had seven sons.

literal: Jihai styled Yuanquan, among the brothers most renowned, post Governor of Luozhou.
idiomatic: Jihai, styled Yuanquan, was the most celebrated of the brothers and became Governor of Luozhou.

literal: Jihai's wife was Minister of Works Li Chong's daughter, Emperor Zhuang's maternal cousin, granted noble rank Lady of Tangjun.
idiomatic: Jihai's wife was Li Chong's daughter, Emperor Zhuang's cousin on the maternal side, and was granted the title Lady of Tang Commandery.

literal: Power lay with Erzhu, disaster about to begin; they urged Jihai to take an outer post to avoid the slightest taint.
idiomatic: As the Erzhu clan seized power and disaster loomed, friends urged Jihai to take a provincial post and avoid the capital.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang's calamity came, Jihai indeed because he was in the provinces escaped.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang fell, Jihai escaped precisely because he was away in the provinces.

literal: Following Emperor Xiaowu into the Pass, enfeoffed Prince of Fengyi, post Secretariat Director, Inspector of Yongzhou, promoted Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, was enfeoffed Prince of Fengyi, became Secretariat Director and Inspector of Yongzhou, then Minister of Works.

literal: Died of illness, posthumous title Solemn.
idiomatic: He died of illness and received the posthumous title Solemn.

literal: Son Heng, styled Deliang, also named Xiaocai.
idiomatic: His son Heng, styled Deliang, also called Xiaocai.

literal: Encountering Zhou and Qi divided, he was several years old, with his mother Lady Li in Luoyang.
idiomatic: When Zhou and Qi split the realm he was still a child, living in Luoyang with his mother, Lady Li.

literal: Qi Shenwu because Heng's father was in Guanzhong confined him tightly.
idiomatic: Northern Qi detained him because his father was in Guanzhong.

literal: His mother then claimed freezing hunger, obtained to take food at Tangyin, entrusted to great magnate Li Changshou, carrying Heng and several orphaned nephews, reaching Chang'an.
idiomatic: His mother pleaded cold and hunger, gained leave to seek food at Tangyin, entrusted herself to the magnate Li Changshou, and brought Heng and several orphaned nephews to Chang'an.

literal: Zhou Wendi as son of a meritorious minister treated him with great courtesy.
idiomatic: Zhou Wendi treated him with great courtesy as the son of a meritorious house.

literal: In late Datong, inherited the fief Prince of Fengyi, repeatedly promoted Inspector of Xunzhou, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Pingliang.
idiomatic: Late in Datong he inherited the fief of Prince of Fengyi, rose to Inspector of Xunzhou, and was re-enfeoffed Prince of Pingliang.

literal: When Zhou received the mandate, by precedent demoted to duke.
idiomatic: When Zhou took the mandate, his rank was reduced to duke by precedent.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate, from Governor of Luozhou summoned as Director of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, he summoned Heng from Luozhou to be Director of Ceremonies.

literal: Soon sent out as Inspector of Weizhou; in office eight years, transformation greatly harmonized.
idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Inspector of Weizhou; in eight years he transformed the region thoroughly.

literal: Citing old age and illness begging bones, officials and people went to the gate memorializing to retain him, the emperor sighed long.
idiomatic: When he begged leave on grounds of age and illness, officials and commoners thronged the palace gate to ask that he stay; the emperor sighed at length.

literal: That year Heng because of grave illness again requested return to the capital; the emperor ordered envoys bring medicine, ask after his condition, envoys visible on the road one after another.
idiomatic: That year, gravely ill, Heng again asked to return to the capital. The emperor sent envoys with medicine and inquiries, one after another on the road.

literal: Died at home, posthumous title Proclaimed.
idiomatic: He died at home, posthumous title Proclaimed.

literal: Prince of Chenliu Qian was Gegen's son.
idiomatic: Prince of Chenliu Qian was Gegen's son.

literal: At the beginning of the state's founding, granted noble rank Duke of Chenliu.
idiomatic: At the founding of the state he was enfeoffed Duke of Chenliu.

literal: With Prince of Wei Yi broke the Qufu tribe, followed attacking Weichen.
idiomatic: With Prince of Wei Yi he broke the Qufu tribe and followed in the attack on Weichen.

literal: Murong Bao came to raid; Qian cut off his left wing, Bao defeated.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao raided, Qian severed his left wing and Bao was defeated.

literal: Murong Chui grievously angry came to Sanggan; Qian was brave but underrated the enemy, died in battle at Chen.
idiomatic: Murong Chui came to Sanggan in fury. Qian was bold but contemptuous of the foe and fell in battle at Chen.

literal: Qian's bearing was towering and outstanding, martial strength unmatched; each time his spear was too fine and short he made large ones, still worried they were light, again hung bells under the blade.
idiomatic: Qian was a towering figure of matchless strength. Finding his spears too slender, he forged heavier ones; still deeming them light, he hung bells beneath the blades.

literal: His bow strength doubled ordinary men.
idiomatic: He drew bows twice as strong as other men.

literal: Because of this extraordinariness, the capital armory constantly kept and recorded them.
idiomatic: Because of their strangeness, the capital armory kept specimens on file.

literal: Qian often used the spear to stab people, penetrating and raising high.
idiomatic: Qian often ran his spear through an enemy and lifted the body on the shaft.

literal: Also once with one hand planted the spear in the ground, spurred the horse pretending retreat; enemies scrambled to seize it, pulled but could not draw it out.
idiomatic: Once he planted his spear in the earth with one hand, feigned retreat on horseback, and when foes rushed to seize the weapon they could not pull it free.
